ADR-001, ADR-004, ADR-005, ADR-010 and ADR-011 are all DRAFT_REQUIRED. The rules in this repository are the proposal of a design at IN_REVIEW.

authority_status: The scaffold was built under a direct operator instruction, recorded in badf/authority.yaml under granted.repository_scaffold. That is an operator instruction recorded by an agent; it is NOT the expiring implementation grant from a business authority seat that the P0.2 design requires. Every other authority in that file is NOT_GRANTED, wp_001_acceptance included, and the registry is now parsed and cross-checked against the state file so that neither a forged section nor a silent disagreement between the two survives validation. Pushing this branch and updating pull request #1 are both inside tool_authority.may; pushing to main is not, and main has not been touched.

recovery: Read AGENTS.md, then badf/authority.yaml, then badf/current-state.json and badf/next-actions.json. The branch is motor/p0.2/repository-and-boundaries off 062a0f7c1b350e4af695978b238b28e323b7d0e0 on main, and pull request #1 tracks it. First safe command: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm verify, which runs the eight checks after it in order. All nine rows above were observed at this head. If any fails, the tree has diverged from this checkpoint and the answer is RECOVERY_REQUIRED, not a fix.
declared_non_coverage: Negative control 6 of the P0.2 design: a push straight to main and a merge with a failing check. Needs branch protection, which is a human record. Unobserved.
The runtime half of every control. Nothing runs: there is no server, no database and no configuration.

The migration lint is a text check over SQL, not a parser. It handles double-quoted identifiers, unqualified names, search_path and plurals, and it now denies by default on an unmodelled DDL statement; it CANNOT see through a dollar-quoted function body, a DO block, dynamic SQL built at runtime, or an extension that creates objects as a side effect. An earlier version of this file called the lint conservative by design, which was affirmatively wrong.

Deny-by-default is triggered by a statement OPENING with CREATE, ALTER or DROP. GRANT, REVOKE, COMMENT ON, SECURITY LABEL, IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA, SELECT ... INTO and CALL are therefore outside it: they are not treated as DDL, so a statement of that shape passes for want of a target rather than failing for want of one. This is a new limit introduced alongside the new rule, stated here rather than left for the next reviewer to find.

The authority registry parser reads the status: line and nothing else. It does NOT read expires_at, so a grant whose expiry has passed still reads as GRANTED to every check in this repository, including the one recorded as UNBOUNDED_PENDING_REVIEW. Expiry is enforced by a human reading the file, not by an instrument.

Rule 7's outbound host allow-list does not exist. The P0.2 design makes it a check of its own and control 10's second half a CI check; neither is implemented, and apps/ contains only a README, so rule 7 binds nothing outside the fixture. This is a CI-side gap, not covered by the runtime-control disclaimer above.
The contract lint over openapi/ and events/. Both directories are reserved and empty; the rules are P0.8 and P0.9.
The observability tests. The baseline is P0.11.
The security proof suite over tests/security/. The BT-G1 matrix needs BT-G0 first.
No fixture proves the typecheck fails, so the compiler is an unwitnessed instrument.

CI runs one Verify job with sequential steps, not the nine independently required checks the design names, and there is no Build job. The merge-blocking effect is equivalent; the divergence is recorded rather than hidden.

The mutation check covers the dependency rules and the migration lint. It does NOT mutate the record validator, the registry reader or the module-package check, so those three are tested by their own suites but not mutation-tested. The round-two authority-registry validator falls in that set, which is worth naming because it is the check that guards authority.
Rules 1 and 2 are generated per module; the fixture exercises one instance of each family, not all four.

The design's control 7 says the boundary check's GENERATION step catches a package with no registry row. It does not; a separate script does. Different instrument from the one specified, recorded here rather than glossed.
